chunks: "Have you come," said they, "to turn us back from what we found our ancestors doing, so that the two of you may attain supremacy in the land? We shall not believe in what you say."

key_terms.لِتَلْفِتَنَا: to turn us back / to divert us

ai.seo_question: Why did the people of Jonah reject his message?
ai.summary: In this verse, the people of Jonah (Yunus) reject his call to repentance, accusing him and his companion of seeking political dominance and trying to divert them from the traditions of their forefathers. Shia exegetes often highlight this as a classic example of *taqlid* (blind imitation of ancestors), where pride in heritage overrides rational acceptance of divine truth. Their dismissal underscores the recurring theme in the Quran that prophetic messengers were frequently viewed as political threats rather than spiritual guides.
